The box does not need it: both services read `/etc/goldrush-*`, outside the synced tree, which is where the leg's own `sed -i` writes.** ⚖️ **SEVERITY NOT INFLATED, AND TWO SCARIER READINGS ARE REFUTED: the county LEDGER IS SAFE — it lives at `/opt/goldrush-ledger/` (`ledger-backup-pull.mjs:7`, runbook `:100`–`:108`), a SIBLING of the synced dir, so no rsync under `/opt/goldrush/` can reach it; and `node_modules` IS SAFE — rsync protects excluded names from `--delete` by default. The leg also gets one thing RIGHT that any rewrite must keep: `server/` (what `goldrush-ledger.service` RUNS, runbook `:60`) is MISSING from the runbook's own allowlist and the denylist syncs it. Fail-open is correctly built — all three arms declare which path they took.** ❓ **NOT VERIFIED AND UNCLOSEABLE FROM THIS DISK: the box's actual tree was not enumerated (that needs ssh to production, which a fire has no authorization for), so the full `--delete` blast radius over hand-placed files remains UNKNOWN.** 🚫 **NO CURE AUTHORED, FOR THREE REASONS: §7.3 routes any deployment act to the OWNER (F-2297-1's own restraint note says so, and this leg IS its option (b)); attended landed it five minutes before this fire and may still be iterating (Mistake #6); and THE OBVIOUS CURE IS SUBTLY WRONG — switching to the runbook allowlist while keeping `--delete` would DELETE `/opt/goldrush/node_modules` on a git-less box, since with an explicit source list it is neither in the source nor exclude-protected. A fire that "fixed" this in passing would break the assayer the attended session just built to unblock launch week.** ➡️ **ONE WORD: (a) minimum — add `--exclude .env.local`, strictly subtractive, removes the secret, cannot break the sync · (b) full — the runbook allowlist PLUS `server/`, retaining `--exclude node_modules --exclude dist --exclude .git` so `--delete` cannot strip the box · (c) leave it and sync by hand per the runbook. Recommendation (a) TODAY then (b)** — (a) is safe under any reading and takes one line; (b) ends the 7.7 GB and the denylist rot. ⓘ Also worth a word: the second `ssh` (`sed`+`systemctl restart`) has `BatchMode` but NO `ConnectTimeout`, where the probe ssh has `ConnectTimeout=8` — a box that accepts TCP then stalls hangs the deploy unbounded inside a fire's budget. Evidence: `artifacts/f2298-1-deploy-sync-payload/note.md` (reproduce recipe in §8). ✅ **OPTION (a) EXECUTED s2299 at `909d8c4ae` — and TWO OF THIS ROW'S FACTS ARE CORRECTED BY THE EXECUTION, both in the direction of MORE severity, so re-read F-2299-1 before ruling on (b)/(c).** (1) The payload is **FIVE live credentials, not "a live Cloudflare token"** — `.env.local` carries `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and **`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`**, the factory's own Claude subscription credential. (2) **The leg is NOT a divergence from the runbook** — it is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the runbook's own denylist recipe at `:57`, which contradicts the allowlist at `:40`; so the leak predates the leg and lives in the DOCUMENTED HAND RECIPE, widening the exposure window from "since 12:21 today" to UNKNOWN. **(b) and (c) remain fully OPEN and untouched — the 7.73 GB payload question is not answered by this fix, and s2298's warning that an allowlist plus `--delete` would strip `/opt/goldrush/node_modules` was re-verified and still holds.** The `ConnectTimeout` note also remains open.

🔺 **F-2299-1 OPEN, NARROWED 2026-09-24 to the Claude Code token and two local pastes (the desk row at the top) — OWNER (s2299 2026-08-25): THE DROPLET SYNC SHIPPED FIVE LIVE CREDENTIALS, AND THE LEAK WAS IN THE RUNBOOK'S OWN RECIPE, NOT THE NEW LEG — CURED ONE LINE, BUT A COPY MAY ALREADY BE ON THE BOX.** Executing F-2298-1's recommendation (a) on a dry board. **Measured LOCAL and READ-ONLY: no ssh to production, nothing deployed, no credential VALUE read, printed or committed.** 🔑 **CORRECTION 1 — THE PAYLOAD IS FIVE CREDENTIALS, NOT ONE.** `.env.local` (428 B, mode 600, untracked, `.gitignore:3`) carries `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and **`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` — the factory's own Claude subscription credential, i.e. the thing that pays for every fire and every lane runner.** F-2298-1 priced this as "a live Cloudflare token"; the desk was under-informed by four keys. 🔑 **CORRECTION 2, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT MOVES THE DECISION — THE LEG IS NOT A DIVERGENCE FROM THE RUNBOOK.** F-2298-1 read `docs/ops/agenttown-server.md:40`'s allowlist and called the denylist a divergence. **The runbook contains BOTH recipes: an allowlist at `:40` and, at `:57`, a denylist that is BYTE-IDENTICAL to `deploy.sh:170` after normalising whitespace and `--timeout=60`** (verified by extracting both strings from their files and comparing, not by eye). ➡️ **So the exposure is NOT a defect the new leg introduced — it is a defect in the DOCUMENTED HAND RECIPE, which predates the leg and which the owner may have run at any time since the box was set up. The exposure window is therefore not "since 12:21 today"; it is UNKNOWN.** That is why the cure had to land in BOTH files (fix the CLASS, not the instance). ✅ **PROVEN SENT, THEN PROVEN FIXED, BY MEASUREMENT AND NOT BY READING THE EXCLUDE LIST:** a local `rsync --dry-run` reproducing the leg's exact exclude set — **read out of `deploy.sh` at run time rather than retyped, so the probe cannot drift from its subject** — lists `.env.local` in the transfer set pre-cure and not post-cure; **55,661 → 55,660 files, EXACTLY ONE REMOVED**, which is the whole evidence for "strictly subtractive". ⓘ **The probe asserted its own validity first (F-2215-1) and this was not decorative: its first run returned `0 lines` and REFUSED rather than reporting a clean result, because `rsync -n` prints nothing without an itemiser. A probe whose failure mode is an empty list is indistinguishable from good news.** 🛠️ **CURE: `--exclude .env.local` in `scripts/deploy.sh:170` AND in the runbook's `:57` recipe (`909d8c4ae`). Provably safe: nothing box-side reads that file — `goldrush-assay.service` takes `/etc/goldrush-assay.env` (runbook `:32`), `goldrush-ledger.service` uses `EnvironmentFile=/etc/goldrush-ledger.env` (`:60`), both OUTSIDE the synced tree, which is exactly where the leg's own `sed -i` writes; and `grep -rn "env.local" server/ scripts/assay-worker* scripts/ledger*` returns ZERO hits.** `bash -n scripts/deploy.sh` parses clean. ⚖️ **WHY A FIRE ACTED WHERE s2298 CORRECTLY DID NOT, STATED PLAINLY SO THE OWNER CAN VETO IT: s2298's three reasons were re-measured rather than inherited, and two no longer hold.** Its reason (3) — *"the obvious cure is subtly wrong"* — is about the ALLOWLIST rewrite and **explicitly does not apply to (a)**; its reason (2), *"attended may still be iterating"*, is refuted by measurement (`deploy.sh` unchanged since `3ff1eb606`, clean vs HEAD, 30 min quiet). Only §7.3 remained, and **this is not a deployment act** — it is a one-line subtractive edit to a pipeline script, reversible, inside CLAUDE.md §2's directly-implementable set, taken under §7.4 (owner absent + reversible) with this veto line. **It forecloses nothing: (b) and (c) stay fully open.** 🚨 **WHAT THE CURE DOES NOT DO, AND IT BOUNDS THE OWNER'S REMAINING WORK: rsync PROTECTS excluded names from `--delete` — the same property s2298 used to refute the `node_modules` scare — so if any earlier run of the runbook's `:57` recipe already placed `.env.local` on the box, THIS FIX WILL NOT REMOVE IT.** ❓ **UNCLOSEABLE FROM THIS DISK: whether a copy is already there needs ssh to production, which a fire has no authorization for.** **One word, and the first half is a two-minute check: (a) `ssh root@<droplet> 'ls -la /opt/goldrush/.env.local'` — if it exists, `rm` it AND ROTATE ALL FIVE CREDENTIALS, because a token that has sat on a public-IP box is disclosed whether or not anyone read it · (b) treat the box as clean on the grounds that the leg never ran and the hand recipe was never used · (c) rotate regardless, as cheap insurance. Recommendation (a) — it is one command and it converts an UNKNOWN into a fact.** ⓘ **Do NOT read this row as closing F-2298-1: the 7.73 GB payload, the allowlist fork, and the missing `ConnectTimeout` on the second `ssh` are all still open there.** Evidence: `artifacts/f2299-1-env-local-exposure/note.md` (reproduce recipe §5, ~10 s, local, no network).

🔺 **F-2329-1 OPEN — OWNER (s2329 2026-08-26): A VERIFIED, LIVE DEPLOY IS RECORDED AS `interrupted` IN THE ONLY MACHINE-READABLE CHANNEL, AND THE ASSAYER LEG DIED SILENTLY INSIDE IT — SO THE ENGINE/ASSAYER SKEW F-2296-1 NAMES MAY BE LIVE RIGHT NOW.** Measured LOCAL and READ-ONLY on a dry board: no ssh to production, nothing deployed, no credential value read. 📊 **THE TWO CHANNELS DISAGREE, AND ONLY ONE IS MACHINE-READABLE.** `logs/deploy.log` records `08:40:24 DEPLOYED ok https://655390f8.gold-rush-3in.pages.dev`, then `08:40:26 VERIFY attempt 1/7: … says ccedf620`, then `08:40:26 VERIFIED published ccedf620 at https://gold-rush-3in.pages.dev` — that is s2327’s handoff commit `ccedf6200`, live and confirmed against the production alias. `logs/deploy-result.json` records `{"outcome":"interrupted","url":"","publishedBuild":"ccedf620","commit":"ccedf6200…","ts":"2026-08-26T01:43:06Z"}`. ⏱️ **The timestamps are in DIFFERENT ZONES and both are correct, which is why this is easy to misread: the result file writes true UTC (`date -u`, `deploy.sh:19`) while the log writes local (`date '+%F %T'`, `:14`), so `01:43:06Z` IS `08:43:06+07` — i.e. the `interrupted` verdict was written 2m40s AFTER the deploy was verified live.** 🕳️ **THE RUN DIED INSIDE THE ASSAYER LEG, PROVEN BY ABSENCE: the log ENDS at the VERIFIED line, and NONE of the leg’s three declarations appear — `ASSAYER SYNCED` (`deploy.sh:177`), `ASSAYER SYNC FAILED mid-step` (`:179`), `ASSAYER NOT SYNCED (box unreachable)` (`:182`).** The leg is entered at `:174` and the success path exits at `finish deployed 0` (`:184`), so the process was killed between those two lines; the traps at `:43`–`:45` (`HUP`/`INT`/`TERM` → `finish interrupted`) are what wrote a result file at all, and they emit no `note`, so the log gets nothing. ✅ **SAME-DAY INTERNAL CONTROL, SAME BOX, SAME LEG, 100 MINUTES EARLIER — so this is a divergence from a proven baseline, not an untested path: `07:00:14 DEPLOYED ok` → `07:00:15 VERIFIED published d4458867` → `07:00:31 ASSAYER SYNCED: droplet tree + pin d4458867, services restarted`.
